Messages.Author: Oopy Rixx
Messages.Body:
Name: Cautionary Tale
Type: Combat
Requires a ready Sabbat vampire. Only usable when the opposing vampire should go to torpor.
Place Cautionary Tale on this Sabbat vampire. This vampire may burn Cautionary Tale to gain two votes during a referendum. A vampire may have only one Cautionary Tale. If this vampire goes to torpor, burn this card.

Name: Shock And Awe
Type: Combat.
Aim. Play when choosing a strike. Requires a Sabbat vampire.
If any damage from this strike is successfully inflicted on the opposing minion, this Sabbat vampire may burn 1 blood to place this card on that opposing minion. The opposing minion may not cast votes during political actions called by this Sabbat vampire. The opposing minion may remove Shock And Awe as a  action.

Name: Warpath
Type: Action Modifier
Cost: 1 blood
Requires a Sabbat vampire. Only usable as the acting vampire's political action is announced.
If this action is successfully blocked and combat occurs, damaging strikes played by this acting vampire deal 1 additional damage. If this Sabbat vampire is an Archbishop, Priscus or Regent, the blocking vampire also may not dodge or end combat as a strike.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
I like them all.

Cautionary Tale should be reworded:

Requires a ready Sabbat vampire. Only usable when the opposing vampire goes to torpor.

Messages.Author: agzocgud
Messages.Body:
I´d like to see Cautionary Tale as a location with the same mechanic as Alamut instead:

Powerbase: Detroit
Type: Master
Requires a titled sabbat vampire
Cost: 1 pool
Master: unique location.
If a Sabbat vampire you control is ready at the end of combat and the opposing non-sabbat vampire is not, put x counters on this card, where x is half the capacity of the non-sabbat vampire (rounded up). During the referendum of a political action, you may burn X counters from this card to give a sabbat vampire you control X votes for that referendum.

(May need some teakning)

Overkill is highly underrated. You know, like in computor games and such.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
Because it can be a cautionary tale to get nearly forced into torpor as much as it is to actually get sent there. "That guy nearly sent me into torpor!"

Seems to me that it shouldn't be circumvented by Undead Persistence. It's not the 'replacing' effect but more about the idea that if you almost went into torpor you should be more worried about picking fights. It should also work if someone plays Psyche! or Telepathic Tracking after a Rotschreck.

At any rate, the card as written does not require it to be played after combat and it does burn if the vampire playing it goes to torpor; so against an UP deck, they need to survive the rest of the combat as well.
